name: create_event
description:
Create an event in the user's connected Outlook Calendar.

Parameters:
- subject: Event title (required).
- start_time/end_time: Event start and end timestamps (required). Use YYYY-MM-DD for all-day events, otherwise use RFC3339 timestamps with the user's timezone offset from viewer context (e.g. 1970-01-31T12:00:00-08:00). Always include the offset — never send bare datetimes.
- timezone: IANA or Windows timezone for the event (e.g. "America/Chicago", "Pacific Standard Time"). Defaults to UTC.
- description: Optional event body/notes (plain text).
- location: Optional location name.
- attendees: Optional list of email addresses to invite.
- is_online_meeting: Set to true to create a Teams meeting link.
- is_all_day: Set to true for all-day events (start/end should be dates like 2026-04-28T00:00:00).
- recurrence: Optional recurrence pattern. Must include "pattern" and "range" objects.
  Pattern types:
    "daily" - repeats every N days.
    "weekly" - repeats on specific days of the week (use "daysOfWeek": ["monday", ...]).
    "absoluteMonthly" - repeats on a fixed date each month (use "dayOfMonth": 15 for the 15th).
    "relativeMonthly" - repeats on a weekday position each month (use "daysOfWeek": ["tuesday"], "index": "second" for the second Tuesday).
    "absoluteYearly" - repeats on a fixed date each year (use "dayOfMonth" and "month").
    "relativeYearly" - repeats on a weekday position each year (use "daysOfWeek", "index", and "month", e.g. last Friday of November).
  The "index" field accepts: "first", "second", "third", "fourth", "last".
  Range types: "noEnd" (repeats forever), "endDate" (stops at "endDate"), "numbered" (repeats "numberOfOccurrences" times).
  Example (daily, no end): {"pattern": {"type": "daily", "interval": 1}, "range": {"type": "noEnd", "startDate": "2026-04-30"}}
  Example (weekly Mon/Wed/Fri): {"pattern": {"type": "weekly", "interval": 1, "daysOfWeek": ["monday", "wednesday", "friday"]}, "range": {"type": "noEnd", "startDate": "2026-04-30"}}
  Example (second Tuesday of every month): {"pattern": {"type": "relativeMonthly", "interval": 1, "daysOfWeek": ["tuesday"], "index": "second"}, "range": {"type": "noEnd", "startDate": "2026-04-30"}}
  The range.startDate MUST match the date portion of start_time.

If the user has a request relative to today, like "create an event for tomorrow" or "schedule for next week",
compute the actual timestamps for start_time and end_time rather than using relative words.

The result contains the created event's event_id and details.

start_time.description: Start time as RFC3339 with timezone offset (e.g. 1970-01-31T12:00:00-08:00), or YYYY-MM-DD for all-day events. Always include the user's timezone offset from viewer context.

end_time.description: End time as RFC3339 with timezone offset (e.g. 1970-01-31T13:00:00-08:00), or YYYY-MM-DD for all-day events. Always include the user's timezone offset from viewer context.

timezone.description: IANA or Windows timezone (e.g. "America/Chicago"). Always provide this.

attendees.description: List of attendee email addresses to invite.

is_online_meeting.description: When true, a Microsoft Teams meeting link is added to the event.

is_all_day.description: When true, creates an all-day event.

recurrence.description: Recurrence pattern for recurring events. Must have "pattern" (with type and interval) and "range" (with type and startDate). See tool description for examples.
